note: Public research for the incident desk, not findings from Patchriot assessments. The report’s 40 list entries are combined into 28 distinct cases. Sources were checked on 12 November; the newer Cisco BroadWorks exploitation acknowledgement is included. Advisory dates refer to disclosure or listing, not an inferred attack date. Testing perspectives are editorial assessments, not guarantees that Patchriot would detect or prevent a breach. This file is not loaded or published automatically. Refresh existing PHP2Shell, Railway, LiteLLM, Brotli, Cisco ASA/FTD and eMudhra records rather than publishing duplicate entries; preserve other earlier catalogue records.

entries.title: PHP2Shell request-state memory corruption
entries.summary: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 let malformed request handling corrupt PHP memory before application checks can protect it. Unauthenticated server code execution is possible.
entries.takeaway: Install PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 or 8.5.12, or a later supported fix or verified vendor backport; restart affected workers.

catalogue.qualifying: Disclosure: 21 Oct; CISA exploitation listing: 26 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Install PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 or 8.5.12, or a later supported fix or verified vendor backport; restart affected workers.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Affected web-serving PHP runtimes include PHP-FPM and mod_php. A vulnerable installation is not proof of compromise; the cited sources provide no aggregate victim or loss total.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: dependency review helps identify known exposure. Discovering the original memory defect needs specialist fuzzing or source review; ordinary website checks cannot promise it.

entries.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain
entries.summary: Volexity reconstructed a chain crossing authentication, file-handling and privilege boundaries on a then-patched VPN appliance. The attackers sought directory credentials and recovery keys and removed logs.
entries.takeaway: Apply current Ivanti chain fixes and investigate suspected compromise. Volexity links the 29 October privilege-escalation patch; do not rely on a clean integrity check alone.

catalogue.qualifying: Activity from 3 Oct; report: 13 Oct; patch update: 29 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Apply current Ivanti chain fixes and investigate suspected compromise. Volexity links the 29 October privilege-escalation patch; do not rely on a clean integrity check alone.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Observed on Connect Secure 22.8R2.4. CVE-2026-104935 covers the entry flaws; CVE-2026-111357 covers the later privilege-escalation fix. Wider victim counts remain unknown.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: request-routing and authorization review are relevant, but reproducing an appliance exploit chain requires specialist scope and investigation.

entries.title: Plex media-server takeover chain
entries.summary: Plex reports active attacks combining SSRF, internal API access, owner-token exposure and file writing. The chain permits execution as the media-server process; miners and traffic proxies were observed.
entries.takeaway: Update to 1.43.3.10861 or later. If compromise is suspected, rebuild cleanly, invalidate sessions and change the account password.

catalogue.qualifying: Exploitation update: 19 Oct; public proof of concept: 16 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Update to 1.43.3.10861 or later. If compromise is suspected, rebuild cleanly, invalidate sessions and change the account password.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Internet-reachable servers before the fixed build are at risk. The vendor gives no infected-host count or total financial loss.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: internal-service access and token boundaries merit review. A scoped read-only website assessment does not reproduce the file-write or execution stages.

entries.title: Zeabur cloud and customer-secret compromise
entries.summary: Zeabur says stolen internal credentials opened access to clusters, customer servers and a platform database. How the attacker first acquired those credentials remains unconfirmed.
entries.takeaway: Rotate exposed credentials and inspect or rebuild affected hosts. Remove public administrative access and shorten credential lifetimes.

catalogue.qualifying: Activity: 14–15 Oct; preliminary report: 19 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Rotate exposed credentials and inspect or rebuild affected hosts. Remove public administrative access and shorten credential lifetimes.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The vendor records root sign-ins to 101 GCP servers and access to environment-variable records. Machines, accounts and records are different measures; they must not be added as one victim count.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: cloud IAM and internal-network separation need a broader review than a public URL test. No claim is made that Patchriot would have prevented the breach.

entries.title: Railway environment-secret exposure
entries.summary: Railway describes unauthorized internal access and exposure of encrypted environment secrets, with some decrypted. Detailed exploit mechanics and the final customer-specific scope were not disclosed in the preliminary account.
entries.takeaway: Follow Railway’s rotation guidance, replace affected variables and tokens, and review account and registry activity.

catalogue.qualifying: Activity: 20–22 Oct; preliminary report: 22 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Follow Railway’s rotation guidance, replace affected variables and tokens, and review account and registry activity.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Railway estimated possible variable exposure in at most 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000. Precautionary provider-key resets affected more users; a reset alone does not prove theft.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: review internal service permissions and secret boundaries. These are infrastructure controls beyond a normal external website assessment.

entries.title: LiteLLM malicious release artifacts
entries.summary: An exposed administrative key remained valid and led to theft of an organization-owner GitHub token. Attackers changed publishing workflows and released credential-stealing LiteLLM 1.107.0 artifacts.
entries.takeaway: Rebuild affected environments from verified clean artifacts, rotate accessible secrets and verify the vendor’s replacement signing keys and digests.

catalogue.qualifying: Malicious release: 21 Oct; canonical attack account: 23 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Rebuild affected environments from verified clean artifacts, rotate accessible secrets and verify the vendor’s replacement signing keys and digests.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Affected packages and container images are described by the vendor. A clean source tag does not establish that published binaries were clean. No confirmed infected-host total is supplied.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: release provenance, least-privilege CI tokens and actual key revocation matter. Public website checks cannot establish build-pipeline integrity.

entries.title: PingCAP internal data and source-code exposure
entries.summary: PingCAP says stolen service-account credentials enabled copying internal records and source code. Exposed material included SQL-editor text, account associations and encrypted API-key values.
entries.takeaway: Follow customer-specific notifications and review exposed credentials and access. PingCAP reports revoking identified credentials and closing access paths by 14 October.

catalogue.short_name: PingCAP internal data and source-code exposure
catalogue.qualifying: Activity: 9 Sep–7 Oct; disclosure: 19 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Follow customer-specific notifications and review exposed credentials and access. PingCAP reports revoking identified credentials and closing access paths by 14 October.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The vendor reported no evidence that data stored in TiDB was impacted. That finding does not negate the separate internal-data exposure; individual customer scope remained under investigation.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: service-account permissions and cloud separation require infrastructure access to examine properly. No actual loss total is established here.

entries.title: Collabora built-in CODE command injection
entries.summary: CVE-2026-110447 allows unauthenticated commands through the Nextcloud built-in CODE proxy while its server is stopped, including restart or crash windows.
entries.takeaway: Upgrade richdocumentscode to 26.4.303 or later, or remove it. Disabling the app alone is insufficient.

catalogue.qualifying: Advisory: 14 Oct; CISA exploitation listing: 23 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Upgrade richdocumentscode to 26.4.303 or later, or remove it. Disabling the app alone is insufficient.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The affected component is Nextcloud’s built-in CODE app. Standalone Collabora Online is excluded. Neither the advisory nor the exploitation listing gives a victim total.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: lifecycle states matter. Testing only a healthy running application can miss a failure path; source review complements runtime checks.

entries.title: Brotli decoder memory corruption in Node.js
entries.summary: CVE-2026-111497 lets malformed compressed input corrupt decoder memory. Applications processing attacker-controlled Brotli data may crash, disclose memory or execute code.
entries.takeaway: Use Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or newer supported fixes. Check other runtimes that bundle Brotli separately.

catalogue.short_name: Brotli decoder memory corruption in Node.js
catalogue.qualifying: Node.js release: 21 Oct; CISA listing: 27 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Use Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or newer supported fixes. Check other runtimes that bundle Brotli separately.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Node.js 22, 24 and 26 were affected. Known exploitation of the component does not establish that every Node.js application was attacked.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: dependency inventory and decoder fuzzing are relevant. Ordinary external HTTP checks cannot prove a native-memory parser is safe.

entries.title: GPUStack loopback trust bypass
entries.summary: CVE-2026-102895 treats requests appearing to come from loopback as administrator requests. A local reverse proxy or spoofed real-IP header can expose administrative APIs without credentials.
entries.takeaway: Upgrade beyond 2.2.0; use 2.2.2 or newer to cover the separate SAML flaw too. Inspect unexpected administrator keys and worker changes.

catalogue.qualifying: CISA exploitation listing: 9 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Upgrade beyond 2.2.0; use 2.2.2 or newer to cover the separate SAML flaw too. Inspect unexpected administrator keys and worker changes.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The maintainer records exploitation of a 2.1.1 deployment. Administrator access can expose provider secrets and permit worker execution; wider victim counts are unknown.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: check authorization through the deployed proxy path. A trusted network location must not substitute for authenticated identity.

entries.title: IBM Aspera Faspex privilege escalation
entries.summary: CVE-2026-123218 allows a crafted application message to bypass authorization and obtain administrator privileges in Faspex 5.0.0–5.0.19.
entries.takeaway: Install 5.0.19 PL1 and verify faspex-core build 1ce4b13, Fix Pack 1. IBM lists no workaround.

catalogue.qualifying: IBM bulletin: 7 Nov; CISA listing: 9 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Install 5.0.19 PL1 and verify faspex-core build 1ce4b13, Fix Pack 1. IBM lists no workaround.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: IBM’s prose requires an authenticated user, while its score vector says otherwise. This entry follows the prose and CISA description; confirmed victim totals are unavailable.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: compare ordinary-user and administrator access to the same operations, including permission-changing fields.

entries.title: Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN denial of service
entries.summary: CVE-2026-76418 can reload affected appliances through unauthenticated SSL VPN input when the relevant secondary-authentication configuration is present.
entries.takeaway: Use Cisco’s branch-specific fixed-release table. Do not weaken secondary authentication as a permanent substitute for patching.

catalogue.short_name: Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN denial of service
catalogue.qualifying: Advisory: 28 Oct; CISA listing: 29 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Use Cisco’s branch-specific fixed-release table. Do not weaken secondary authentication as a permanent substitute for patching.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The established effect is service disruption, not demonstrated data theft or code execution. Exposure depends on the VPN and tunnel-group settings.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: configuration and version review are appropriate. Deliberately crashing a live VPN is outside a non-destructive website assessment.

entries.title: Cisco BroadWorks XML file disclosure
entries.summary: CVE-2026-20320 lets unauthenticated OCI-P XML requests make the parser resolve external entities and disclose files readable by the BroadWorks service.
entries.takeaway: Upgrade affected BroadWorks components to RI.2026.07 or later. Cisco lists no workaround.

catalogue.qualifying: Disclosure: 19 Aug; KEV: 10 Nov; Cisco confirms exploitation: 12 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Upgrade affected BroadWorks components to RI.2026.07 or later. Cisco lists no workaround.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Application Delivery Platform, Application Server, Profile Server and Xtended Services Platform are listed. Cisco’s 12 November update supersedes its earlier no-known-exploitation statement.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: review XML parser configuration and authorization. The update confirms exploitation, but gives no victim count or loss total.

entries.title: eMudhra weak intermediate certificate keys
entries.summary: Google corroborated weak randomness in keys for eight subordinate CA certificates. A client still trusting those keys could accept a forged HTTPS identity.
entries.takeaway: Ensure trust stores, browser protections and bundled certificate validators receive current vendor updates; check each application’s actual validation path.

catalogue.qualifying: Reported to Google: 17 Oct; response: 20 Oct; update: 4 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Ensure trust stores, browser protections and bundled certificate validators receive current vendor updates; check each application’s actual validation path.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Google found no CT-logged certificates chaining to the six TLS intermediates before blocking them. This limits demonstrated impact against CT-enforcing clients; it is not a count of compromised endpoints.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: a website check cannot establish the integrity of an external CA’s private-key generation. Client trust-store maintenance is a separate responsibility.

entries.title: GPUStack unverified SAML identities
entries.summary: CVE-2026-102894 issues sessions from SAML identities without validating the response. The callback can remain reachable even when SAML is not configured.
entries.takeaway: Upgrade to 2.2.2 or later. Block the callback temporarily if upgrading is delayed; disabling SAML alone does not address the vulnerable route.

catalogue.qualifying: GitHub advisory listing: 10 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Upgrade to 2.2.2 or later. Block the callback temporarily if upgrading is delayed; disabling SAML alone does not address the vulnerable route.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: GPUStack versions from 0.7.1 to before 2.2.2 are affected. Existing administrator identities may be impersonated; the cited advisory does not establish malicious exploitation.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: verify signatures, replay handling and disabled-provider routes. This is distinct from the loopback authentication flaw.

entries.title: GitLab regular-expression compiler RCE
entries.summary: CVE-2026-110264 is an integer overflow reached while compiling a crafted regular expression. Under affected conditions, an unauthenticated caller may execute code on GitLab.
entries.takeaway: Install the applicable fixed GitLab branch: 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 or 19.5.1, or a later supported release.

catalogue.qualifying: Critical patch release: 21 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Install the applicable fixed GitLab branch: 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 or 19.5.1, or a later supported release.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The advisory supplies affected ranges for CE and EE. Published detection rules do not by themselves establish a successful malicious compromise.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: source-assisted fuzzing and dependency review are relevant; routine web checks cannot promise discovery of native compiler memory bugs.

entries.title: React Server Components payload handling
entries.summary: CVE-2026-126187 can permit server execution in rare response paths combining multiple typed arrays with attacker-controlled data. React applications without RSC support are excluded.
entries.takeaway: Upgrade the affected react-server-dom packages to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 or 19.3.1 on the appropriate branch and redeploy.

catalogue.qualifying: GitHub advisory listing: 10 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Upgrade the affected react-server-dom packages to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 or 19.3.1 on the appropriate branch and redeploy.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The affected transports are webpack, parcel and turbopack. The cited advisory establishes exposure, not observed malicious attacks or a victim total.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: review actual server serialization paths and dependencies. A client-only React site must not be labelled vulnerable just because it uses React.

entries.title: Kubeflow shared-pipeline upload authorization
entries.summary: CVE-2026-77596 omits authorization for empty-namespace HTTP uploads in multi-user Pipelines. A low-privilege caller can inject shared pipeline versions that other tenants may later execute.
entries.takeaway: Apply the maintainer’s fixed release and matching manifests, including commit 62516d8c525f. Inspect shared pipeline versions and scheduled runs.

catalogue.qualifying: GitHub advisory listing: 9 Nov; upstream fix: 9 Sep.
catalogue.fix: Apply the maintainer’s fixed release and matching manifests, including commit 62516d8c525f. Inspect shared pipeline versions and scheduled runs.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The fixed Go module revision is 0.0.0-20260909234119-62516d8c525f. Direct API exposure can widen access. No malicious victim total is established.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: compare HTTP and gRPC authorization and check empty or omitted namespaces. Triggering another tenant’s workload is not part of ordinary read-only testing.

entries.title: Mongoose count-query selector injection
entries.summary: CVE-2026-125120 leaves countDocuments queries outside sanitizeFilter protection. User-influenced count filters can change query meaning and reveal information, depending on application use.
entries.takeaway: Update to Mongoose 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3 or 9.9.2 on the respective branch, or a newer supported fix.

catalogue.qualifying: GitHub advisory listing: 10 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Update to Mongoose 6.13.11, 7.8.12, 8.24.3 or 9.9.2 on the respective branch, or a newer supported fix.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The application must expose a relevant filter path. The advisory does not establish remote code execution, known victims or a financial-loss figure.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: compare count and retrieval behavior under account boundaries. A library version alone does not demonstrate a reachable application vulnerability.

entries.title: Tor relay hosts altered to intercept SSH
entries.summary: Tor operators reported compromised Linux hosts whose configurations were changed to intercept SSH traffic, including turning non-exit relays into exits. The initial host-entry path remained under investigation.
entries.takeaway: Review relay configuration and host evidence. Follow Tor’s recovery guidance, rebuild compromised hosts and replace exposed identities and credentials.

catalogue.short_name: Tor relay hosts altered to intercept SSH
catalogue.qualifying: Tor Project warning: 5 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Review relay configuration and host evidence. Follow Tor’s recovery guidance, rebuild compromised hosts and replace exposed identities and credentials.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Tor reports rejecting affected relays. The notice does not establish a Tor protocol flaw or publish a compromised-host total.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: this needs host and network investigation. A public web application assessment cannot validate relay-host integrity.

entries.title: SharePoint deserialization and authentication chain
entries.summary: CERT-EU describes active exploitation of CVE-2026-50522 within a series of SharePoint flaws involving deserialization and authentication. Published accounts disagree on whether authentication is required for that entry.
entries.takeaway: Apply the relevant Microsoft security updates, investigate exposed servers and rotate potentially exposed credentials.

catalogue.qualifying: CERT-EU July exploitation advisory, released 23 Jul.
catalogue.fix: Apply the relevant Microsoft security updates, investigate exposed servers and rotate potentially exposed credentials.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Affected on-premises products include Subscription Edition, Server 2019 and Enterprise Server 2016. This is not a blanket statement about SharePoint Online.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: appliance-specific source review and known-flaw validation complement web testing. The cited notice does not establish a complete victim inventory.

entries.title: Oracle PeopleTools management RCE
entries.summary: CVE-2026-35273 affects the HTTP Updates Environment Management component and can permit remote execution without credentials.
entries.takeaway: Follow Oracle’s PeopleSoft patch-availability guidance for the affected branch. Detailed patch installation information requires Oracle Support access.

catalogue.qualifying: Oracle security alert: 10 Jun.
catalogue.fix: Follow Oracle’s PeopleSoft patch-availability guidance for the affected branch. Detailed patch installation information requires Oracle Support access.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: PeopleTools 8.61 and 8.62 are listed. Oracle did not test unsupported releases; absence from the table does not make them safe. The alert does not establish malicious exploitation.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: check exposure of management interfaces and applicable versions. Discovery of the underlying execution flaw can require deeper research.

entries.title: Atlassian Data Center file disclosure
entries.summary: CVE-2026-21589 lets unauthenticated callers read specific known-path files inside affected web roots. It does not provide general directory listing.
entries.takeaway: Apply the product-specific patched release in Atlassian’s table; investigate exposure of sensitive files in the application root.

catalogue.qualifying: Disclosure: 5 Oct; CISA exploitation listing: 15 Oct.
catalogue.fix: Apply the product-specific patched release in Atlassian’s table; investigate exposure of sensitive files in the application root.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Affected server products include Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible and Fisheye. Atlassian says Cloud was patched and its investigation found no Cloud exploitation evidence.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: review path normalization and access to known sensitive resources. Do not infer that all filesystem paths or every Atlassian deployment were exposed.

entries.title: Adobe Commerce and Magento authorization bypass
entries.summary: CVE-2026-71362 can grant elevated access to sensitive resources without authentication. The affected and fixed versions vary across Commerce and Magento branches.
entries.takeaway: Install the corresponding August 2026 security build from APSB26-92 or a later supported fix.

catalogue.short_name: Adobe Commerce and Magento authorization bypass
catalogue.qualifying: Bulletin: 11 Aug; CISA exploitation listing: 24 Sep.
catalogue.fix: Install the corresponding August 2026 security build from APSB26-92 or a later supported fix.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: The earlier vendor statement about no known attacks predates CISA’s listing. Neither source provides a total of compromised stores or losses.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: compare anonymous, customer and administrator permissions at application endpoints. Avoid assuming a visible storefront reveals the authorization of its backend.

entries.title: WSO2 JWT authentication bypass
entries.summary: The vendor describes CVE-2026-5430 as accepting JWTs signed with unsupported algorithms, permitting account or administrator takeover.
entries.takeaway: Apply the public fixes or the appropriate supported update level for the listed WSO2 product and branch.

catalogue.qualifying: Vendor disclosure: 3 May; later CISA listing: 24 Sep.
catalogue.category: Disclosed flaw with later exploitation notice
catalogue.fix: Apply the public fixes or the appropriate supported update level for the listed WSO2 product and branch.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: API Manager and listed Control Plane, Traffic Manager and Universal Gateway releases are affected. CISA’s mechanism description conflicts with the vendor; this entry follows the vendor for the flaw and CISA only for listing status.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: verify token algorithms and signatures across protected routes. The older disclosure is included for the later exploitation notice, not presented as a new November discovery.

entries.title: Pocket ID stale email-verification token
entries.summary: CVE-2026-115770 allows an old verification token to mark a changed email address as verified. Downstream takeover depends on applications trusting email-based account linking.
entries.takeaway: Upgrade the backend to revision 0.0.0-20260727180059-43aaccd5bfac or a later fix; invalidate tokens when their bound address changes.

sources.label: Pocket ID advisory and fixed revision

catalogue.qualifying: GitHub advisory listing: 9 Nov.
catalogue.fix: Upgrade the backend to revision 0.0.0-20260727180059-43aaccd5bfac or a later fix; invalidate tokens when their bound address changes.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: An ordinary account and the relevant account-edit settings are required. Applications linking solely by stable OIDC subject are excluded from the downstream email-linking consequence.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: review account changes and relying-party identity links, not only the login form. No malicious victim count is established by the advisory.

entries.title: GitLab group SAML account takeover
entries.summary: CVE-2026-6552 could let a GitLab EE group Owner take over another group member’s account through SAML identity management.
entries.takeaway: Install GitLab 18.10.8, 18.11.5 or 19.0.2, or a later supported fix.

catalogue.qualifying: Patch release: 10 Jun.
catalogue.fix: Install GitLab 18.10.8, 18.11.5 or 19.0.2, or a later supported fix.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Group Owner privileges are a precondition. The release does not establish malicious exploitation.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: group administration should not grant control of members’ personal identities.

entries.title: GitLab Analytics Dashboard stored XSS
entries.summary: CVE-2026-10087 lets a developer-role GitLab EE user inject dashboard content that executes as a targeted viewer.
entries.takeaway: Install GitLab 18.10.8, 18.11.5 or 19.0.2, or a later supported fix.

catalogue.qualifying: Patch release: 10 Jun.
catalogue.fix: Install GitLab 18.10.8, 18.11.5 or 19.0.2, or a later supported fix.

sections.label: Affected systems and evidence
sections.body: Victim interaction is required. The release supplies no confirmed victim total.

sections.label: Testing perspective
sections.body: Our assessment: examine stored content across contributor and viewer roles. This differs from the separate SAML identity flaw.
